subject: Tenant data safeguards and learning policies — clarifying retention & deletion
messages:
From: Alex Liu <alex@catalystai.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@catalystai.com
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant data safeguards & learning policies — quick clarifications

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Catalyst AI is close to a decision and one of our final legal/security checks is around how vendor platforms treat customer content. We have three short areas we need clear, written answers for legal: 

1) Training usage: do you ever use customer-submitted text, logs, or embeddings to train or improve any models in your catalog (including internal benchmarking/evals)? If so, under what contractual terms and opt-ins?

2) Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for (a) request/response logs, (b) KV/cache snapshots, (c) backups/snapshots and long-term archives? Are there region/residency differences for EU data?

3) Deletion mechanics: for a customer-initiated deletion request, what is the end-to-end timeline, and do you provide a deletion certificate and audit log? Is there an API we can call to purge everything programmatically?

I've attached our security questionnaire (Security-questionnaire.pdf) with some of the fields prefilled. Can you point me to the right person at Redwood to get formal language for the DPA addendum?

Appreciate a short, bulletized reply or a 30-min sync this week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Catalyst AI
security@catalystai.com

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Liu <alex@catalystai.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant data safeguards & learning policies — quick clarifications

Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers below; Marissa (privacy) and Neha (security ops) are looped for formal wording and any contract language. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you prefer.

1) Training usage
- By default, Redwood does not use customer content (requests, responses, embeddings) to train or update our production model weights.
- We may run aggregate, anonymized telemetry analyses for service quality (e.g., to detect regressions in latency or quota anomalies), but that data is not used to change model parameters.
- Any use of customer data for model training or fine-tuning is explicitly opt-in and performed only under a written agreement (we've done this in rare cases as a dedicated managed service).

2) Retention windows (defaults)
- Request/response logs: 30 days (short-term operational logs used for troubleshooting and SLO metrics).
- KV/cache state: ephemeral; in-memory caches are cleared after sessions and are not persisted to long-term storage.
- Backups/snapshots: persistent snapshots are retained for up to 90 days by default for recovery; longer retention can be contractually specified.
- EU residency: customers who elect EU region keep data resident in EU regions; retention windows are the same unless otherwise negotiated.

3) Deletion mechanics
- Initiation: Customer requests via the support portal, the Delete API endpoint, or through your account rep.
- Execution: Active tenant data removed within 7 business days. Backups and snapshot purges may take up to 60 days depending on replication and backup windowing.
- Certification: We provide a deletion report and audit log showing objects removed — delivered as a signed artifact.
- Programmatic purge: Yes — we expose an authenticated Delete API for supported plans; Dedicated/Private deployments have admin tooling and procedural steps.

Attachments: I attached our internal playbook for the deletion flow (redwood-data-deletion-playbook.pdf) to outline steps and timelines in more detail.

If you want contract language for the DPA, Marissa will follow up with suggested clauses and the contact at Legal.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Liu <alex@catalystai.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant data safeguards & learning policies — quick clarifications

Thanks Dylan — that helps. A couple of follow ups from our security team: 

- Model evaluation logs: when you say "telemetry analyses," does that include storing input/output pairs that are used to evaluate model quality? If so, are those ever written to persistent storage?
- Edge/replica caches: Catalyst runs some traffic through edge nodes in EU; are there transient copies of KV caches or snapshots outside the primary region during failover/replication?
- Deletion SLA: our procurement needs firm timelines (e.g., "active data within 5 business days, backups within 45 days"). Is Redwood willing to commit to a shorter deletion SLA for enterprise contracts?

Also, can you add a legal contact so we can propose DPA language? Prefer someone who can speak to EU data residency language and certification delivery.

Appreciate the quick turn here. If easier, open a calendar for tomorrow morning and we'll take 30 min.

Alex

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Liu <alex@catalystai.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant data safeguards & learning policies — clarifying retention & deletion

Alex — looping in formal responses and suggested DPA language. Below are the clarified points and a proposed SLA you can include in procurement. I'm including some explicit contract-friendly wording you can copy into your draft.

Quoted: "On Thu, 16 Aug 2028 at 08:47 AM Alex Liu <alex@catalystai.com> wrote:"
> - Model evaluation logs: when you say "telemetry analyses," does that include storing input/output pairs that are used to evaluate model quality? If so, are those ever written to persistent storage?

Answer:
- We do persist anonymized evaluation artifacts only when running controlled evals, and only with customer consent. Those artifacts are stored in isolated buckets, labeled for the evaluation project, and retained under the project-specific retention schedule (commonly 90 days unless otherwise agreed). We do not incorporate such artifacts into general model training.

> - Edge/replica caches: Catalyst runs some traffic through edge nodes in EU; are there transient copies of KV caches or snapshots outside the primary region during failover/replication?

Answer:
- KV caches are in-memory and transient; we do not persist per-tenant KV caches to cross-region long-term storage. For high-availability purposes we replicate state metadata (not full cache contents) to regional failover nodes. Persistent snapshots used for disaster recovery are stored only in the regions you select and follow the residency choices in the account.

> - Deletion SLA: our procurement needs firm timelines (e.g., "active data within 5 business days, backups within 45 days"). Is Redwood willing to commit to a shorter deletion SLA for enterprise contracts?

Answer:
- We can commit to contractually shorter SLAs for enterprise agreements. Typical options we offer: Active tenant data purge within 3 business days (enterprise SLA), backup/snapshot purge within 30–45 days depending on snapshot cadence, and certified deletion report delivered within 5 business days after purge completion. Exact timelines are scoped per deal.

Proposed DPA language (copy/paste friendly):
"Vendor shall not use Customer Content to train or improve its production models unless Customer provides explicit, written opt-in. Vendor shall retain Customer Content only as necessary to provide services and in accordance with the retention schedule set forth in Exhibit A. Upon Customer request, Vendor shall delete Customer Content and associated backups and provide a deletion certificate and audit log. Backup deletion may require up to 45 days to accommodate snapshot and replication windows, unless a different timeline is agreed in writing."

Next steps:
- Marissa will send a redline of DPA Exhibit A and sample SLA today.
- Dylan: I'll hand the proposed language to Legal; please include the HubSpot ticket (HS-57892) and we'll attach the deletion playbook for your security team.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

PS: For Private or Dedicated deployments we can provide more immediate purges as part of the deployment checklist; contact neha_kapoor for operational runbook alignment.
